candidate_role: Creature copy engine and scalable token generator
commander_specific_hypothesis: Magecraft triggers when an instant or sorcery is cast OR copied. Anhelo’s casualty copy therefore yields another Fractal token sized by that spell’s mana value; for the common 2+ mana spells these bodies qualify as future casualty-2 fodder.

combo_prerequisites_verified: Relevant Anhelo casualty-copy/copy-resolution interaction checked; not a deterministic combo claim.

baseline_result: Talrand only triggers on casts and makes a 2/2 flying Drake; Anhelo’s copy does not count as a cast for Talrand.
variant_result: One Deekah trigger from the original cast and another from Anhelo’s casualty copy; two Fractals whose +1/+1 counters each equal that spell’s MV.
sample_size_and_uncertainty: Oracle/rules and role analysis; no qualified gameplay comparison; EDHREC snapshot is corroborating only.
decision_reason_or_rejection_reason: Deekah maps more directly to Anhelo’s defining cast-and-copy pattern than Talrand. Trade-off: five mana versus four, and Fractals do not have flying; Deekah can grant a token unblockability for {3}{U}. Its color identity is blue only: green/blue words describing the produced token do not add green to the card’s identity.
reviewer_notes: Current EDHREC Optimized snapshot: Deekah 23% (39/173), Lift 45; retrieved 2026-10-13. Card rulings explicitly say copies of instants/sorceries cause Magecraft.

slot_or_package: copyable multi-opponent creature control / casualty value
commander_specific_hypothesis: Anhelo can copy this four-mana sorcery by sacrificing a creature with power 2+. The copy resolves first; each opponent makes piles and the controller chooses one pile to sacrifice; after that resolves, the original makes opponents re-pile their remaining creatures, allowing a second sacrifice selection.

baseline_result: Talrand's Invocation creates two 2/2 flying Drakes; Anhelo can copy it to create four Drakes total.
variant_result: The copy and original each make every opponent separate their current creatures into piles, with you choosing the pile that player sacrifices.
sample_size_and_uncertainty: Oracle, current legality and stack order checked; no board-state/gameplay sample; pile decisions and opponents’ boards make impact variable.
decision_reason_or_rejection_reason: The deck retains Army of the Damned, Baral and Kari Zev, Judith, Lagomos, Ghoulish Procession, Poppet Stitcher, and the new Deekah token engine. Swapping away Talrand’s Invocation gives up a strong four-Drake casualty payoff but adds broad, non-targeted creature control that is itself unusually rewarding when copied.
